In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TBB, BAL and whole blood should be investigated in order to detect HCMV in LT recipients.
the use of TBB in the diagnostic approach of HCMV pneumonia should be considered, but further studies are warranted to confirm the role of this technique.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCMV detection in TBB may be useful to detect HCMV pneumonia, while HCMV detection and quantification in BAL is not useful in this context.
HCMV investigation on TBB could be useful for evaluating posttransplanted complications.
HCMV detection in TBB is more sensitive than BAL for the diagnosis of HCMV pneumonia, but the latter is a more sensitive test to detect HCMV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of HCMV in TBB from LT recipients could be a reliable tool to evaluate post-transplant complications.
